A

Adrian NE
Latin Hadrianus, “from Hadria.” One of Aurelia’s six fellow students at departure. His ship is heavily laden for an important, distant flight (7). See also: Seven Students.
Adrian Alte-Jung NE
The literary psychologist who writes Aurelia as Little Eva and Goldilocks: A Study of the Golden Doll Archetype. Albert Derby criticizes his fragmentary archetypal theories and hostility to the golden-doll figure (85–86). The surname plays on old and young and recalls C. G. Jung. See also: Books about Aurelia.
Aerated Flesh SP
Aurelia’s flesh contains air, and her bones are hollow. These observations appear in Cipher’s study of her physiology, which also describes her control of body temperature and her electric outer skin (92–93). See also: Bird Bones, Electric Skin, Cipher.
Agrionia CA
Greek: a festival of Dionysus celebrated at Orchomenus, involving ritual pursuit of women. Among the ancient festivals the Prince of Nysa grafts onto Aurelia’s cavalcade: “They had old elements of the Agrionia, of the Dionysia, of the Lenaea or new-wine feast, of the Anthesteria or flower festival.” The Agrionia commemorated the daughters of Minyas, who were driven mad for refusing to worship Dionysus. → See also: Dionysia, Lenaea, Anthesteria, Prince of Nysa
Ailanthus Tree ET
Ailanthus altissima, commonly called tree of heaven. On the final night, a woman gives Aurelia seeds to swallow so that a tree will grow from her body. A year after her burial, the tree appears. Its smell and beauty recall Aurelia, but the people have forgotten her (178, 182). See also: Words on Water, Antlers.
Albert Derby NE
The reviewer whose survey of ten books about Aurelia appears in the Morning Review on her third morning on the world. His review occupies pages 81–98, before the three-day walking journey begins. See also: Books about Aurelia, Morning Review.
Aldous Spencer-Trencher NE
The philosopher who brings Aurelia a bowl of Slowpoke Snails at the Third Ientaculum. He explains her seven-day sickness as the local world’s destructive response to an alien visitor (158). His name suggests Aldous Huxley and Herbert Spencer; a trencher is a plate or serving board. See also: Strange World Sickness, Doctor Thorgrimsson, Slowpoke Snails.
Ambrosia / Honey Wine CA
Greek ambrosia, the food of the gods. The Prince of Nysa identifies the mulsum served at the First Prandium as wine made with the special honey once used in ambrosia. He initially refuses it to Clootie’s unroyal camp; Aurelia commands him to send a jug (115). See also: Mulsum, Olympians, Prince of Nysa.
Anthesteria CA
Greek: the “flower festival” celebrating Dionysus in Athens during the month Anthesterion (February-March). Among the ancient festivals grafted onto Aurelia’s cavalcade. The Anthesteria celebrated the opening of new wine and included rituals for the dead, appropriate for a visit that will end in death. → See also: Agrionia, Dionysia, Lenaea
Anti-world SP
A companion planet on the opposite side of a world’s orbit. The novel describes such worlds as difficult for their own counterparts to see. Clootie claims to come from Shining World’s dark companion and later calls the visited world itself an anti-earth (53–54, 147). See also: Dark Companion, Cousin Clootie.
Antikenladen ET
German, “antiques shop.” Herr Boch’s expensive antique business. During the Second Ientaculum, a double handful of artifacts brought down by Aurelia’s monkey expands into enough merchandise to fill six pavilions (102, 133). See also: Herr Boch, Monkey.
Antlers SP
Herr Boch’s returning growths turn out to be antlers, which Aurelia distinguishes from horns associated with evil. They signify unusual intellectual achievement. He had suppressed the growths with Blue Caustic. On the final night they fall off; Aurelia swallows them, and branched antlers later grow at her burial place (130–31, 179–80, 182). See also: Herr Boch, Blue Caustic, Ailanthus Tree.
Aphthonica SP
Greek aphthonos: “without envy, abundant.” Called “World Abounding,” one of the seventy-six planets approved for Aurelia’s World Government assignment. Characterized by “an impudent artiness.” The name suggests excessive plenty that has curdled into artistic pretension. → See also: Seventy-Six Planets
April Fool ET
The Kansas City Star places the arrival just after midnight on April Fool’s Day and treats it as a recurring visitation hoax. Its account also reports an escaped convict found dead at the landing site (39–40). See also: Prairie Dog Town Prolocutor.
Ariadne CA
Greek mythology: daughter of King Minos, helped Theseus escape the labyrinth. One of the Prince of Nysa’s past lovers. He boasts: “Ariadne was already dead before I first had her. It was a good, but creepy, relationship that we had.” This allusion connects the Prince to Dionysus, who in myth married Ariadne after Theseus abandoned her, and in some versions, after her death. The Prince’s necrophilic confession marks him as genuinely ancient and morally compromised, even as he serves Aurelia. → See also: Prince of Nysa, Carya, Leucippe
Arthur Airim NE
Author of The Mathematics of the Aurelian Curve, reviewed by Albert Derby. His analytical geometry purports to read character and fate, and his account emphasizes the sudden termination of Aurelia’s curve (90–91). See also: Books about Aurelia.
Athanatos Bark ET
Greek athanatos, “deathless.” A substance Herr Boch sells for thirty thousand dollars an ounce. The Prince of Nysa has used it for centuries; it also sustains a fragment of Uncle Silas. Aurelia declines it after hearing about the tedium and painful contradictions of a life prolonged beyond its proper end (161–62). See also: Prince of Nysa, Uncle Silas.
Audry NE
One of Aurelia’s six fellow students from Shining World. She “took flight” before Aurelia during Kickoff Night. The name is a variant of Audrey, from Old English æðelþryð meaning “noble strength.” → See also: Seven Students
Aunt Caladium ET
Caladium: a tropical plant with colorful leaves. One of Aurelia’s disguises. “Aurelia slipped, in an Aunt Caladium disguise, back into the luxury cabin, and then she left off the disguise and was herself.” The botanical name suggests decorative camouflage: bright leaves hiding her true identity. → See also: Roxie, Potlatch
Aurelia NE
A feminine Latin name associated with aureus, “golden.” A fourteen-year-old student from Shining World. Her week on the visited world culminates in a three-day walking ministry organized around twelve meals. Beloved but technically forgetful, she preaches happiness and dies alongside Cousin Clootie. See also: Shining People, World Government Course.
Aurelian NE
Adjective form of Aurelia, used in book titles: Machiavelli and the Aurelian Ethos, The Mathematics of the Aurelian Curve, The Aurelian Revival. Also references Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, Roman Emperor AD 270–75, who restored the empire after crisis, suggesting Aurelia’s role as restorer. → See also: Books About Aurelia

B

Bad Music League ET
An organization that publishes Is Aurelia Saint Cecelia?, a book arguing she is the patron saint of music incarnate. “The Bad Music League is not a tongue-in-cheek group. It is a genuine tongue-in-the-bugle-mouthpiece organization.” They appreciate Aurelia’s discordant horn music, which others find cacophonous. → See also: Saint Cecelia, Books About Aurelia
Balthasar Doppiocroce NE
The surname suggests Italian doppia croce, “double cross.” A magus who joins Rex Golightly beside the river during the Second Cena. As a young prince, he projected a butterfly ego-fragment and was fined for apparently eating it. He inherited the throne the next morning and pardoned his own debt (151–53). See also: Magi, Ego-Fragment Projection, Rex Golightly.
Bandicoot SP
One of the seventy-six planets approved for Aurelia’s World Government assignment. Uncle Silas claims to have served in “the second invasion of Bandicoot.” Characterized by “a wildness that is worse than horror.” A bandicoot is a small marsupial; the mundane animal name deflates cosmic grandeur. → See also: Seventy-Six Planets, Uncle Silas
Basso-parlante SP
Italian: “speaking bass.” Rex’s voice type: a deep, resonant speaking voice. Distinguished from singing voice; suggests operatic classification applied to everyday speech. The Shining People have developed specialized voice registers for their “operatic-conversevole” mode of discourse. → See also: Contralto, Operatic-conversevole
Bearded Like a Pard LR
An allusion to the soldier in Shakespeare’s As You Like It, act 2, scene 7. A pard is a leopard. The phrase describes Uncle Simon, also called Silas, on Aurelia’s first morning at Potlatch (43). See also: Uncle Silas.
Big Bang RA
The cosmological origin point that Aurelia connects to the Law of Happiness. Charles Greenpasture asks: “Was the ‘Big Bang’ the birth of both God and the Universe?” Aurelia’s teaching holds that “There was one law given at the physical beginning of the universe, at the ‘big-bang’ moment—the Law ‘Be Happy!’” → See also: Law of Happiness, Charles Greenpasture
Big Blow RA
The Prince of Nysa’s cosmology: “The whole universe swarmed out of a horn that was blown quite by accident. Astronomers know it as the ‘Big Blow.’” A parody of Big Bang cosmology merged with horn-of-plenty mythology. Aurelia denies this account. → See also: Prince of Nysa, Horn
Bird Bones SP
Cipher’s study reports that Aurelia’s bones are hollow and full of air, as observed through a Jefferson’s Fluoroscope (92). The report ultimately identifies her with the broad human race despite physiological differences. See also: Aerated Flesh, Jefferson’s Fluoroscope, Cipher.
Black Tarsier Mechanism SP
Cousin Clootie’s mechanical servant, the dark counterpart to Aurelia’s monkey. “Cousin Clootie had a black tarsier-like mechanism with bright eyes that went up to his ship and back on errands. It didn’t fool around and it didn’t pull monkey-shines.” A tarsier is a nocturnal primate with enormous eyes; Clootie’s version is mechanical, efficient, and humorless, unlike Aurelia’s playful monkey that “steals” artifacts and pulls pranks. → See also: Cousin Clootie, Monkey
Blaise Genet NE
French: Blaise (from Latin Blasius, “lisping”); Genet (a small carnivore, or French for “broom plant”). A young man on the River Boat who wins a game of brag against Karl Talion, claiming four quarts of blood. He is “made nervous by the constant knocking at doors and windows,” a man of uncertain identity. His surname may also allude to Jean Genet, French author of transgressive literature. → See also: Brag, River Boat, Karl Talion
Blue Caustic ET
A powder “used on cattle after they are dehorned. It prevents new growth of core-matter.” Herr Boch used it for years to suppress his horn growth but stops during Aurelia’s peripateticus, allowing antlers to sprout. The substance connects animal husbandry to human transformation. → See also: Antlers, Herr Boch, Horned People
Bolide ET
Greek bolis: “missile,” from ballein “to throw.” A bright meteor or fireball. Aurelia is repeatedly called a “bolide” in the newspapers, both a celestial phenomenon and something thrown at Earth. The Prairie Dog Town Prolocutor warns of “contagious bolides that have struck our world.” Aurelia herself announces: “I’m a bolide.” The ballad-makers ultimately sing “She was a Bolide” with horn accompaniment as she dies, reducing her cosmic significance to astronomical trivia. → See also: Prairie Dog Town Prolocutor, Worm with the Pistol
Books about Aurelia PM
Ten books reviewed by Albert Derby on Aurelia’s third morning, before the walking journey (81–98):
  1. Aurelia Is from Iowa: The Waterloo Revelations, by Hawk-Eye the Reporter.
  2. Is Aurelia Saint Cecelia?, by the Board of Presidents of the Bad Music League.
  3. Aurelia as Little Eva and Goldilocks: A Study of the Golden Doll Archetype, by Adrian Alte-Jung.
  4. How Well Does She Govern? The Crux of the Matter, by Charles Sinkman.
  5. Machiavelli and the Aurelian Ethos, by Kirol Grabman.
  6. The Mathematics of the Aurelian Curve, by Arthur Airim.
  7. All That Glitters Is Not Gold: The Underworld and Floating-World Connections of Aurelia, by Jimmy Candor.
  8. How Human Is Aurelia? Bird Bones and Basal Metabolism, by Cipher.
  9. Will It Ever Be Fun Again? The Aurelian Revival, by the Board of Governors of Romp Publications.
  10. How Square Must We Be? The Implications of Acceptance and Humility, by the Free Spirit Daily.
Brag ET
A card game played on the River Boat with blood as stakes. “The card game they were playing was ‘brag,’ and a man named Blaise Genet had been winning the hand.” Brag is a real British card game similar to poker, involving bluffing. The blood-stakes transform social gaming into ritual sacrifice. → See also: River Boat, Blaise Genet, Karl Talion
Bust Rust LN
The rust-removing product in Aurelia’s account of minimal government. Governmental machinery may grow rusty through disuse, but an oilcan, Bust Rust, and a hammer should remain available when action is needed (110). See also: Circuit-Court.

C

Carya CA
One of the Prince of Nysa’s former lovers, remembered as turning into a walnut tree: “Carya, she was always turning into a walnut tree, and indeed she had a walnut tree in her lineage. Talk about a woman with wooden responses!” The recollection reinforces the Prince’s association with Dionysus (102). → See also: Prince of Nysa, Ariadne, Leucippe
Cavalcade ET
Italian cavalcata: a procession on horseback. Aurelia’s traveling court, combining elements of Roman triumph, Dionysian procession, and medieval progress. “It was a parade. It doesn’t take much to start a parade.” The cavalcade includes five thousand persons, musicians with discordant horns, Long-Horn cattle, and participants in ancient festival costumes. → See also: Peripateticus, Dionysia
Cena RM
Latin, the principal Roman meal. The fourth meal of each day in Aurelia’s walking journey. At the Third Cena she speaks about death as passage into a larger room and grace as the key to that passage (174–75). Her cosmic Law of Happiness homily belongs to the preceding Third Merenda. See also: Ientaculum, Prandium, Merenda.
Charles Greenpasture NE
A speculative theologian who asks Aurelia about God’s relation to the universe, divine goodness and power, and the Big Bang. Clootie interrupts with his Zero Equation. Aurelia challenges Greenpasture’s bilateral model and proposes a billion-lateral one (55–57). The name recalls the green pastures of Psalm 23. See also: Big Bang, Zero Equation.
Charles Sinkman NE
Author of How Well Does She Govern? The Crux of the Matter. He gives Aurelia thirteen points out of a hundred, against an average of eight for the governments he surveys. His book reconstructs beliefs he thinks she would express, including the road-map, gift-of-happiness, and four-corner-prayer formulations (86–90). See also: Books about Aurelia, Law of Happiness.
Cheap-Shotting LN
Aurelia calls this “the besetting offense of this world” in her Second Cena homily. She attacks slander, defamation, and the sale of hatred as pleasure, then demands the tongues and ears of the worst offenders. The resulting barrel includes animal parts supplied in mockery (153–55). See also: Hate-Em-Ails, Jimmy Candor.
Children of the Penumbra SP
Failed Shining World students who “do not come back, and yet live somewhere for many years. They form a sort of penumbra that is always partisan to the golden world. If you cannot be true ‘Children of Light,’ perhaps the next best is that you should be ‘Children of the Penumbra.’” The penumbra is the partial shadow zone around an eclipse; these are beings of partial illumination. → See also: Golden People, Strange World Sickness
Chthonic Movement ET
Greek chthonios, “of the earth.” The supposed inexorable process invoked by a spectator to excuse the children’s impending deaths. He calls them accidents and says experts are present to study them (178). The phrase shifts responsibility from human actors to an allegedly unstoppable force. See also: Strange World Sickness.
Cipher NE
The pseudonymous author of How Human Is Aurelia? Bird Bones and Basal Metabolism. The study describes her bones, aerated flesh, electric aura, and variable temperature. It also reports variation in recordings of her speech (92–94). See also: Books about Aurelia, Electric Skin.
Circuit-Court ET
One of the many names for Aurelia’s traveling governance: “a circuit-court, an ambling assize.” The term evokes both American frontier justice (judges riding circuit) and electrical circuits: governance as current flowing through the land. → See also: Peripateticus, Cavalcade
Citizens’ Execution League ET
An assassination group distinct from the Kill Aurelia Now League. Its members make speeches and attempt to kill Clootie, including with a point-blank .45 shot, but his ship intercepts the attacks. Jimmy Candor earlier threatens a “Citizens’ Execution” in his press campaign (136, 172, 180). See also: Forbidden Phrase Law, Jimmy Candor.
Cock-Crow LN
The morning signal for Ientaculum. The Prince of Nysa threatens a reluctant rooster into crowing: “The terrified cock crew for the early Ientaculum breakfast.” The cock-crow connects to Peter’s denial of Christ and signals the boundary between night and day, sleep and waking. → See also: Ientaculum, Prince of Nysa
Cogency Scan SP
A diagnostic Aurelia proposes comparing with Marco’s when he worries that they are different kinds of people. He does not know what it is. She next asks him to count his chromosomes (137). See also: Marco Rixthaler, Shining People.
Compensating Contingency Grid SP
A navigational device Aurelia forgets to construct. Patmo reminds her to set it at departure, prompting her confession that she never made it. It is one of three omitted instruments, alongside the Monitory Chronometer and an unnamed third device (7, 9). See also: Monitory Chronometer, Kickoff Night.
Compensation, The RA
The completed event whose unique world Herr Boch claims this is. Aurelia counters that several other worlds claim the same status. In the novel’s Christian framework, it suggests the Incarnation and redemption (131). See also: World of the Compensation, Rome.
Constancy, Law of Planetary SP
A doctrine holding “that all planets are approximately equal in their potential, all of them from ‘Shining World’ to Skokumchuck. It states that the people on the grubby worlds are just as smart as those on the bright worlds, though sometimes they have poor ways of showing it.” The law challenges Shining World superiority while excusing earthly failures. → See also: Grubby, Shining World
Constructive Defamation LN
One of Jimmy Candor’s oxymoronic phrases, along with “dynamic apathy,” “creative loitering,” “dark-sides advocacy,” “precursor reporting,” “macho cookery,” and “compassionate hatred.” The terms expose his bad faith through self-contradiction. → See also: Jimmy Candor, Cheap-Shotting
Contralto SP
Italian: the lowest female singing voice. Lavender’s voice type: she speaks “in her easy contralto.” Applied here to speaking voice rather than singing, part of the Shining People’s operatic-conversevole discourse. → See also: Basso-parlante, Operatic-conversevole
Cornutus Covens ET
Latin cornutus: “horned.” The ritual circles of the Horned People. “The ‘horned people’ of a coven or cornutus encircle a victim and then they close in. There are horrid screams. Then the ‘horned people’ draw back again, and the victim is dead in the middle of their old stamped and trampled circle.” → See also: Horned People, Blue Caustic
Corporate Communion RA
Cousin Clootie’s teaching on the purpose of money: “Don’t you people know what money is for? It is for the corporate communion of all the people in the world. . . . There is no absolute or personal ownership of money, not ever. Money is like office. It may be occupied and administered, but it may not be owned.” Misuse of money is “gluttony or obesity”: “Taking into oneself more money than one needs is as bad as taking into oneself more food than one needs. Corporations of persons demanding more money than they need are corporations of persons demanding damnation for themselves and deprivation for others.” The term “corporate communion” connects economic justice to eucharistic theology. → See also: Cousin Clootie, Division of Mission
Counter-action SP
A Shining People defensive technique. When three men try to throw Aurelia off the River Boat, “Aurelia took quick reprisal and counteraction, and Helen was also involved. One of the men himself went into the churning water and was drowned. One of them lay on the deck in a broken posture.” → See also: Instrumental Knot
Cousin Clootie NE
Auld Clootie is a Scots name for the Devil, associated with the cloven hoof. Aurelia’s dark counterpart and fellow governor, fifteen years old to her fourteen. He claims to come from Shining World’s dark companion and serves people she overlooks. Both die when a deflected yin-yang dart lodges in him and then strikes Aurelia as she bends over him (147, 173–74, 180–82). See also: Dark Companion, Division of Mission.
Cube of Virtues RA
Aurelia’s analogy for the unity of virtue: “There are not virtues. There is only virtue. We cannot have some of the particular virtues without having them all. To lack even one of the six particular virtues is like having a geometrical cube lacking one of its six sides. Without one of its sides, it wouldn’t be a cube at all.” When told Earth counts seven virtues, she exclaims: “Aw blacksnake blood! How am I going to come up with a regular seven-sided figure to use for analogy?” The cube image derives from Aquinas’s teaching on the unity of the cardinal virtues (ST I–II, q. 65). → See also: Aquinas, Law of Happiness

D

Dark Antagonist SP
A term for Cousin Clootie in his adversarial aspect, opposing Aurelia while serving a parallel governing function. → See also: Cousin Clootie, Dark Counterpart
Dark Companion SP
A shadow planet paired with a bright primary on the opposite side of a shared orbit. Clootie says he comes from Shining World’s dark companion; Helen calls it SHOK-994. He also says the visited world is itself a dark companion whose people cannot perceive their bright primary (53–54, 143, 147). See also: Anti-world, Dark Companion SHOK-994.
Dark Companion SHOK-994 SP
Clootie’s claimed world of origin. “Cousin Clootie is from ‘Dark Companion SHOK-994’ where everything goes wrong.” The catalog-style name (astronomical notation) gives scientific credibility to the shadow-world concept. → See also: Cousin Clootie, Dark Companion
Dark Counterpart SP
The formal designation for Cousin Clootie’s relationship to Aurelia. Every bright governor may have a dark counterpart; the pairing suggests Manichean cosmology. → See also: Cousin Clootie, Anti-world
Daytime Constellations SP
Constellations appear by daylight during Aurelia’s cavalcade. Later the narrator contrasts their visibility above her camp with their absence above Clootie’s, although the two camps are only half a mile apart (108, 148). See also: Cavalcade, Cousin Clootie.
Death-banter ET
The mixture of joking and mortal stakes in the River Boat’s game of brag. The narrator observes that nobody wants to waste a life every night, though the game contains much death-banter (27). See also: Brag, River Boat.
Death-mind SP
The final stage of a Shining People ship’s guidance. Ships follow pilots’ conscious minds, then unconscious minds, then “death-minds” if dead, serving even posthumously. → See also: Oblate Sphere
Dionysia (Greater and Lesser) CA
Greek: festivals honoring Dionysus. The Greater (March) featured dramatic competitions; the Lesser (December) was rural. “At nightfall would come something very like the Greater Dionysia.” → See also: Agrionia, Lenaea, Anthesteria, Prince of Nysa
Division of Mission RA
Clootie’s phrase for his complementary work with Aurelia. She sees higher; he sees lower. He retrieves people and needs she overlooks in the mud, and both acknowledge his harder ministry of repentance (173–74). See also: Cousin Clootie, Governor of Hard Cases.
Dobson City Telegraph PM
A newspaper covering Aurelia’s arrival. → See also: Dobson’s World
Dobson’s World SP
One of the seventy-six planets. Characterized by “an insulting elegance.” → See also: Seventy-Six Planets
Doctor Thorgrimsson NE
Old Norse Þórgrímr: “Thor’s mask.” Medical commentator who writes in Wide Awake, the Morning Medical Journal: “The best thing about this curious encounter is that we may be able to learn something from it.” His measured scientific tone contrasts with the hysteria elsewhere. → See also: Wide Awake
Donkey-Counterpart World SP
Clootie’s revelation about Earth’s cosmic status: “This world does not have a ‘dark companion’ because this world is a ‘dark companion.’ You are standing on an anti-earth and denying that there is an anti-earth. . . . It is the donkey-counterpart world of a horse world, it is the goat world to a sheep world, it is a left-handed world to a right-handed world.” The animal pairings (donkey/horse, goat/sheep) invoke biblical distinctions between the blessed and cursed, the chosen and rejected. Earth’s grubby inhabitants resist this diagnosis. → See also: Cousin Clootie, Dark Companion, Anti-world

E

Ego-Fragment Projection SP
Advanced illusionism technique. Rex projects a fish (“the fluvial and oceanic components of himself”) to write Aurelia’s name on water. Balthasar once projected a butterfly. The skill is “not easy”; Balthasar recognizes Rex’s mastery. The projection can be reabsorbed (“eating” it). → See also: Rex Golightly, Balthasar Doppiocroce
El-Allah-God RA
Rex’s compound name for God in his attempt to save Aurelia through a riddle: “There is no fate, Bait,” Rex says. “There is only El-Allah-God. An esoteric passage that I read lately maintains that God has a secret love for riddles and catch-phrases” (152). → See also: Rex Golightly, Words on Water
Electric Skin SP
A Shining People physical characteristic. People try to determine “what the ‘electric feel’ of her was.” Her surface carries a charge. → See also: Aerated Flesh, Bird Bones
Erigone CA
The Prince of Nysa names Erigone among his past lovers and identifies her with a planet of the Lesser Dog Star (102). The name also belongs to the daughter of Icarius in Greek mythology, linking the Prince’s reminiscence to Dionysian stories. See also: Prince of Nysa, Leucippe, Ariadne.
Eva, Little LR
Reference to Uncle Tom’s Cabin. One book is titled Aurelia as Little Eva and Goldilocks. Little Eva is an angelic child who dies young, like Aurelia. → See also: Books About Aurelia

F

Fat Tom the Sage of the Middle Worlds RA
Aurelia’s named source for her daily insights. The nickname and the teachings on happiness, law, virtue, and grace point toward Thomas Aquinas. The novel relocates this scholastic teaching within its interplanetary setting. See also: Law of Happiness, Final Happiness.
Father of Lights RA
The biblical title for God in James 1:17. It appears in Sinkman’s imagined four-corner prayer and in Aurelia’s Second Ientaculum homily. Jimmy Candor uses her utterance as grounds for demanding legal action and threatening execution (88, 135–36). See also: Forbidden Phrase Law, Charles Sinkman.
Fawney Men ET
Thieves’ cant: sellers of fake jewelry. Merchants selling dubious goods to Aurelia’s cavalcade. She buys a Hyperborean watch that later marks her death-hour. → See also: Hyperborean
Fear and Trembling LR
Allusion to Kierkegaard and Philippians 2:12. Cousin Clootie declares: “I am an advocate of the fear-and-trembling people,” contrasting with Aurelia’s assured salvation. → See also: Cousin Clootie, Home Free Certificate
Final Happiness RA
The ultimate goal in Aurelia’s teachings, distinguished from passing pleasure and present, imperfect happiness. She names its object the Universal Good and connects it with the Father of Lights (111, 135). See also: Law of Happiness, Father of Lights, Universal Good.
Fire-blackened Iron Face NE
Cousin Clootie’s defining physical characteristic. “His was a fire-blackened iron face,” and “the veins of his temples throbbed and crawled as if black lightning were flickering about him, but he showed no emotion.” The image combines industrial forge-work with volcanic darkness, a face hardened by suffering and perhaps by proximity to hellfire. Despite this menacing appearance, “there was nothing at all that anyone could say against him, and he had given them no grounds for suspicion.” → See also: Cousin Clootie, Black Tarsier Mechanism
Floating World ET
The River Boat’s society of gamblers, impostors, and shifting identities. Helen invites Aurelia into this floating world, whose inhabitants claim extraterritoriality and sometimes survive or undo their deaths (24, 33–34). The phrase recalls Japanese ukiyo, the world of transient pleasures. See also: River Boat, Helen Staircase.
Flying Stogies ET
A comic term for cigar-shaped flying objects and the visitation myths associated with them. Newspapers place Aurelia in the “Flying Stogie” category (39, 41). See also: Bolide, Prairie Dog Town Prolocutor.
Forbidden Phrase Law ET
The proposed H.R. 752,996,669, invoked by Jimmy Candor against the phrase “Father of Lights.” He also cites H.R. 752,996,670, the Freedom from Harassment Law. Neither has been finally enacted; both occupy the novel’s absurd deferred category of enforcement if possible (136). See also: Jimmy Candor, Father of Lights.
Forcedmarch, James NE
The “Pan-Math and Science Boluxus” who meets with Aurelia. His surname suggests military urgency toward knowledge. → See also: Pan-Math and Science Boluxus
Four Corners of the Day SP
The four Roman meals structuring Aurelia’s governance: Ientaculum, Prandium, Merenda, Cena. Each “corner” marks a teaching occasion. → See also: Ientaculum, Prandium, Merenda, Cena
Free Spirit Daily PM
The publication credited with How Square Must We Be? The Implications of Acceptance and Humility, the tenth book in Albert Derby’s review (82, 97–98). See also: Books about Aurelia.

G

Gaea SP
Greek: Earth, the primordial goddess. One of the seventy-six planets, “called Telluris or the Earth by its natives.” Characterized by “grossness.” The joke is that Aurelia has landed on Earth itself. → See also: Seventy-Six Planets, World of the Compensation
Gaspar Grootgrondbezitter NE
Dutch: “great landowner.” One of the three Magi serving Aurelia. His name suggests landed wealth. → See also: Magi, Balthasar Doppiocroce, Melchior Rixthaler
Gelotopolia SP
Greek gelos + polis: “City of Laughter.” One of the seventy-six planets, characterized by “juvenile clownishness.” → See also: Seventy-Six Planets
George Clavicle NE
“Forensic Reporter with World International Press.” His name (clavicle = collarbone) suggests anatomical precision. Questions Aurelia’s governance. → See also: World International Press
Golden People / Golden World Cultus SP
“Golden People” is another name used for the Shining People. The “golden world cultus” is the community or culture to which successful students are expected to return. Those who fail may remain loyal to it as Children of the Penumbra without belonging to it again (3–4, 12). → See also: Shining People, Law of Planetary Constancy
Governor of Hard Cases RA
Clootie’s self-designation: “I am the governor of hard cases. I am an advocate of the fear-and-trembling people.” While Aurelia governs through joy and light (“She does things easy”), Clootie governs through repentance and harsh truths (“I do them hard”). He pulls people “out of the mud” that Aurelia cannot see: the ninety-nine depth layers below the surface. The term evokes both pastoral care for difficult souls and legal jurisdiction over complex situations. → See also: Cousin Clootie, Division of Mission, Fear and Trembling
Grabman, Kirol NE
Author of Machiavelli and the Aurelian Ethos. His surname suggests acquisitiveness. Asks Aurelia about “raw-grab” techniques. → See also: Books About Aurelia, Raw-grab
Grace / Love a-burning RA
“The right key that opens the door in the wall is called on one side of it ‘Grace’ and on the other side of it ‘Love a-burning.’ It opens the door even if you use it upside down.” Aurelia’s final homily image for salvation, the key works regardless of approach. → See also: Home Free Certificate, Law of Happiness
Groll’s Planet SP
One of the seventy-six planets, characterized by “grossness.” → See also: Seventy-Six Planets
Grubby / Grubbiness LN
Lafferty’s term for moral and spiritual squalor. Cousin Clootie is “a grubby teenager.” The term extends to worlds; grubbiness is aesthetic and moral failure. → See also: Cousin Clootie, Law of Planetary Constancy

H

Hate-Em-Ails LN
A comic name for people who make hatred a way of life. They appear in Aurelia’s Second Cena denunciation and in the joint celebration that follows, smuggling partisanship into communal enjoyment (154–55). The coinage echoes “hate them all.” See also: Cheap-Shotting.
Hawk-Eye the Reporter NE
Author of Aurelia Is from Iowa: The Waterloo Revelations. The name evokes Iowa’s Hawkeye nickname. Albert Derby’s review describes the author as possibly pseudonymous and treats the documented Iowa-origin thesis as a false conclusion assembled from cultivated evidence (82–83). → See also: Iowa, Iowa Double, Books About Aurelia
Helen Staircase NE
One of the River Boat’s international gamblers. She explains its floating society, later joins Clootie’s camp, and finally kills Marshal-Julio in fulfillment of a card draw. She claims her name means “strong cheese” in German, a joke associated with her description as a cheesecake beauty rather than a literal translation (24, 103, 143, 182). See also: Floating World, River Boat, Marshal-Julio.
Hellpepper Planet SP
One of the seventy-six planets. Characterized by “outright horror.” → See also: Seventy-Six Planets
Herr Boch NE
An antique dealer whose returning growths prove to be antlers rather than the evil-associated horns he fears. He stops suppressing them with Blue Caustic and obtains artifacts from Aurelia’s ship. His antlers fall off on the final night; she swallows them, and they later grow at her burial place (102–3, 130–33, 179–80, 182). His name plays on German Bock, a buck or male goat. See also: Antikenladen, Antlers.
Hokey Planet SP
One of the seventy-six planets. “Any decent person will feel disgust for Hokey Planet.” → See also: Seventy-Six Planets
Home Free Certificate RA
Aurelia’s metaphor for assured salvation, developed in the Third Merenda homily. She can be killed but not ultimately hurt, and the certificate is offered for the asking. Clootie contrasts this with his unsigned certificate of uncertain arrival through many perils (171, 173). See also: Grace / Love a-burning, Cousin Clootie.
Horned People ET
The horned covens or cornutus practice ritual killing through encirclement. Their horns are sensed even when invisible. On the final night they understand Clootie’s shielding well enough to humiliate him without inflicting a fatal blow (172, 179). Aurelia distinguishes their horns from Herr Boch’s antlers. See also: Cornutus Covens, Antlers.
Horner’s Corner SP
One of the seventy-six planets. Characterized by “intolerable raunchiness.” → See also: Seventy-Six Planets
Hound Dog Hulk SP
A world named in the opening ballad and later explicitly ruled out by George Clavicle as Aurelia’s present location (1, 110). The song calls it “Hound-Dog Hulk.” See also: Seventy-Six Planets, Skokumchuck.
Hyades CA
Greek mythology: daughters of Atlas. Visible in daylight during Aurelia’s cavalcade, associated with rain. → See also: Waggoner, Virgo, Dionysia
Hyperborean ET
Greek, “beyond the North Wind.” Aurelia buys a Hyperborean wristwatch that runs when the north wind blows. In the sibyl’s crystal ball, a violent north wind makes the watch display the time of her predicted death after the Third Cena (113–15). See also: Fawney Men.

I

Ientaculum RM
Latin: Roman breakfast, from ientare (“to breakfast”). The first of four daily stops, occasion for “Cock-Crow Insights” and hearing legal cases. → See also: Prandium, Merenda, Cena, Four Corners of the Day
Instrumental Knot SP
Aurelia ties this painful knot in Uncle Gifford Redwing’s anatomy after his assault. A naval knot expert and a doctor cannot resolve it. The proposed solution involves pulling the whole universe through the loop; Aurelia says it can be untied when she leaves the world (46–47). See also: Uncle Gifford Redwing, Counter-action.
Iowa ET
An alternative earthly origin proposed for Aurelia. In Aurelia Is from Iowa: The Waterloo Revelations, Hawk-Eye the Reporter presents documents placing her birth in Waterloo, Iowa, sixteen years earlier. Albert Derby’s review calls the documents genuine but rejects the resulting thesis as false and suggests a murderous conspiracy (82–83). → See also: Hawk-Eye the Reporter, Iowa Double
Iowa Double ET
The “unconscious stand-in” from Waterloo whose documented existence “proves” Aurelia is not from Shining World. “She cannot now be produced because she is supposed to be Aurelia, and there cannot be two of them.” → See also: Iowa, Hawk-Eye the Reporter

J

Jefferson’s Fluoroscope ET
The device cited in Cipher’s study as revealing Aurelia’s hollow, air-filled bones (92). See also: Bird Bones, Cipher.
Jimmy Candor NE
Ironic name: “candor” means frankness, but Jimmy practices malicious distortion. Journalist attacking Aurelia through the Morning Ponder. Practices “constructive defamation” and “dynamic apathy.” → See also: Forbidden Phrase Law, Morning Ponder, Constructive Defamation
Jot-and-Tittle Party LN
The party to which Charles Sinkman imagines Aurelia belonging in his reconstruction of her teaching (88). The phrase alludes to Matthew 5:18 and emphasizes the smallest particulars of the law. → See also: Law of Happiness
Julio Cordovan NE
“The man with a thousand faces” appearing in multiple disguises. First on the River Boat, later as “Marshal Straightstreet.” His surname (Cordovan = fine leather) suggests the wearing of masks or skins. → See also: Marshal-Julio, River Boat

K

Karl Talion NE
Latin talio: “retaliation in kind” (lex talionis). A large man on the River Boat who loses brag to Blaise Genet, surrendering four quarts of blood. Wears “a pleasant mask that was now scarred and tired.” → See also: Brag, River Boat
Kickoff Night SP
The departure ceremony for World Government students. “They were having kick-off night together and giving a rousing send-off to their own adventures.” “Kick-off Nights are always nights of good weather, even if favorable weather must be borrowed.” → See also: Launching Needles, Oblate Sphere
Kill Aurelia Now League ET
Assassination organization that has more than ten million members worldwide within its first hour. Its members resent Aurelia’s supposed superiority and unacceptable views, but chiefly want someone to kill (61–62). → See also: Citizens’ Execution League, Horned People
Kill Cousin Clootie Now ET
Splinter faction with absurdly verbose full name: “Kill Cousin Clootie Now and Aurelia in Just a Minute.” Attacks Clootie on the third night but his protective shafts intercept every blow. → See also: Kill Aurelia Now League, Protective Shaft
Kleptis SP
Greek kleptes: “thief.” One of the seventy-six planets, “one of the Trader planets.” “The dishonesty of the inhabitants of Kleptis . . . was well known.” → See also: Seventy-Six Planets
Kolokynthekephale SP
Greek kolokynthe + kephale: “Pumpkin-Head World.” A legendary, possibly mythical planet. Aurelia fears she’ll end up there; she later asks if she’s landed there and is told no. → See also: Seventy-Six Planets

L

Lamos SP
One of the seventy-six planets. The name may derive from Lamus, king of the Laestrygonians in Homer’s Odyssey, cannibalistic giants. → See also: Seventy-Six Planets
Land Company, Southern ET
Example in Aurelia’s teaching about “raw-grab” corporate takeovers. She explains how to create a “Northern Land Company” as counterpoise, then use media to absorb the target. → See also: Kirol Grabman, Raw-grab
Launching Needles SP
Structures atop which students perch before departure. Ships are “balanced atop launching needles that stabbed into the night sky.” Students sit “like scared crows” during Kickoff Night. → See also: Kickoff Night, Oblate Sphere
Lavender NE
One of the seven students. Speaks in “her easy contralto” and insists: “None of us is lacking, nor can be!” The narrator notes she was mistaken. Name suggests calm, contrasting with her assertive personality. → See also: Seven Students, Contralto
Law of Happiness SP
Aurelia’s central teaching from Fat Tom. Happiness is “both the key and the goal” of existence. “There was one law given at the physical beginning of the universe, at the ‘big-bang’ moment—the Law ‘Be Happy!’” Recognizably Thomistic: Aquinas’s beatitudo. → See also: Fat Tom, Final Happiness, Father of Lights
Lenaea CA
Greek: a festival of Dionysus, the “new-wine feast.” Among the ancient festivals grafted onto Aurelia’s cavalcade. → See also: Agrionia, Anthesteria, Dionysia
Leucippe CA
Greek Leukippe, “white horse.” One of the Prince of Nysa’s past lovers, who, he says, turned into a screech owl. Erigone, another lover in the same reminiscence, belongs to the Lesser Dog Star Clan (102). See also: Prince of Nysa, Erigone.
Lola NE
George Clavicle’s wife. She objects when he writes Aurelia’s obituary prematurely: “She hasn’t gone from us.” Clavicle replies: “She will be gone soon, Lola, just as I have written it here.” Her name (diminutive of Dolores, “sorrows”) suggests grief over his callousness. → See also: George Clavicle
Lotophage SP
Greek lotos + phagein: “Lotus-eater.” One of the seventy-six planets. In Homer, Lotus-Eaters consume a narcotic plant causing forgetfulness. → See also: Seventy-Six Planets
Luxury Cabin ET
Rex Golightly’s hundred-room “tent” called “Potlatch.” Features Spartan dining, chapel, arsenal, moat, game park. “One almost forgot that ‘Potlatch’ had been there less than a week.” → See also: Rex Golightly, Potlatch

M

Magi, The RA
Wealthy patrons who provide gifts and hospitality. The first is Rex Golightly; others include Melchior Rixthaler, Gaspar Grootgrondbezitter, and Balthasar Doppiocroce. The number is left variable, with an early prediction of three, six, nine, or twelve. Their gift-giving evokes Matthew 2, although that Gospel does not specify three visitors. See also: Rex Golightly, Melchior Rixthaler, Gaspar Grootgrondbezitter, Balthasar Doppiocroce.
Marco Rixthaler NE
Melchior Rixthaler’s son, who rides a mule that believes itself a machine and longs to learn how to make living creatures. He buys carnival tickets to kiss Aurelia and later despairs of crossing the differences between their worlds. On the final day, she tells him her objections about chromosomes and other obstacles were jokes; she had wanted a child, but his bashfulness and the little time remaining prevented their relationship (118–19, 137–38, 167–68). → See also: Melchior Rixthaler, Magi
Marshal-Julio NE
Composite name for Julio Cordovan appearing as “Marshal Straightstreet,” Rex Golightly’s supposed bodyguard. Aurelia recognizes him immediately. → See also: Julio Cordovan
Mechano-organo SP
A hybrid of mechanical and organic components. Aurelia made her monkey herself; its awkward construction reflects her uneven practical abilities (118). → See also: Monkey
Media Extinction Arm ET
An assassination faction that uses slow poison. The narrator names Slowpoke Snails as a dish its Jimmy Candor Cell may have poisoned (173). See also: Slowpoke Snails, Jimmy Candor.
Melchior Rixthaler NE
German Reichstaler: a silver coin. One of the three Magi, father of Marco Rixthaler. The coin-derived surname suggests wealth and worldly wisdom. → See also: Magi, Marco Rixthaler
Merenda RM
Latin: light afternoon meal, from merere (“to earn”). Third of four daily stops, between Prandium and Cena. → See also: Ientaculum, Prandium, Cena
Michael Strogoff LR
The blind gambler on the River Boat, seen playing solitaire with blank cards and an Aurelia-value card. He later joins Clootie’s followers. His name recalls Jules Verne’s Michael Strogoff (1876), whose courier survives an attempted blinding. See also: River Boat, Floating World.
Millennians / Millennian Sectarians ET
Religious enthusiasts witnessing Aurelia’s crash-landing. They hail her as “Messianic Angel” and possess “Holy writ” with cabalistic marks. One asks: “Will you make all things new?” → See also: Cavalcade
Monitory Chronometer SP
A timing and navigation device Aurelia forgets to make. Without it she cannot know her proper launch instant or choose the planet best matched to her abilities. Her ship’s programmed network still ensures arrival at one of seventy-six suitable worlds (7–11). See also: Compensating Contingency Grid.
Monkey, The SP
Aurelia’s mechano-organo messenger, badly built. Runs “up and down the dangling ladder from Aurelia’s space ship to herself, bringing her data and assurances.” The invisible ladder blows in the wind. → See also: Mechano-organo, Sky-Rope
Morning Manna RA
Exodus 16: manna in the wilderness. Falls copiously during Day Two but is ignored, “with so much else to eat.” Only breakfast-food companies gather it for adjectives: “fruity, nutty, honey-like.” The miracle passes unnoticed. → See also: Slowpoke Snails
Morning Perspective PM
Newspaper where Nathanial Nutting publishes “Wolf-Children in Perspective,” comparing Aurelia’s arrival to previous media spectacles like “the Bangia Wolf-Children of last autumn.” → See also: Nathanial Nutting, Wolf-Children
Morning Ponder PM
Jimmy Candor’s publication, platform for his attacks on Aurelia. The title suggests contemplative journalism, ironic given his unreflective malice. → See also: Jimmy Candor, Forbidden Phrase Law
Morning Review PM
Publication running Albert Derby’s review of books about Aurelia. → See also: Albert Derby, Books About Aurelia
Mulsum RM
Latin: honey wine. Served at the First Prandium. The Prince of Nysa explains: “It’s honey wine, but of a special honey, the same as we used in ambrosia. The Olympians used it.” → See also: Prince of Nysa, Olympians
Mystery of Iniquity RA
The house obstructing the road in Aurelia’s Third Ientaculum homily. Opening it sends the traveler back a thousand kilometers and a thousand days to Swampy Junction. The name recalls 2 Thessalonians 2:7 (160). See also: Swampy Junction.
Mystery Play CA
The medieval dramatic form onto which ancient festivals are grafted for Aurelia’s cavalcade. “Ritual joys with ancient earth celebrations grafted onto a ‘Shining World’ Mystery Play.” → See also: Cavalcade, Dionysia

N

Nathanial Nutting NE
Journalist who writes “Wolf-Children in Perspective” for the Morning Perspective, comparing Aurelia to past media spectacles. His surname suggests either craziness (“nutty”) or gathering nuts: collecting sensation. → See also: Morning Perspective, Wolf-Children
Nebris CA
Greek: fawnskin worn by devotees of Dionysus. Among ritual attributes at the cavalcade: “the nebris or panther-skin, the fox skins, the she-bear skins.” → See also: Dionysia, Sabazius
New Shansi SP
One of the seventy-six planets. “The dishonesty of the inhabitants of Kleptis or New Shansi was well known.” The New Shansi Old Journal offers sympathetic coverage. → See also: Seventy-Six Planets
Nine Thousand Names of the World LR
Essay Karl Talion is perpetually writing. Echoes Clarke’s “The Nine Billion Names of God,” naming worlds as infinite task. → See also: Karl Talion
Nocastian Nights LR
The marvelous stories Aurelia invokes in her final homily, recalling The Arabian Nights. They contain flying horses, transporting carpets, talking creatures, and other wonders she identifies with the abundance of the real world. She asks what these stories are called locally (174–75). See also: Grace / Love a-burning.
Nomad King ET
Rex Golightly’s self-description: “I am a nomad king as well as a tall tycoon.” Combines wandering with authority, personal rather than territorial power. → See also: Rex Golightly
Nysa CA
Greek mythology: mountain where Dionysus was raised by nymphs. The Prince of Nysa serves as Aurelia’s master of ceremonies. Nysa was traditionally located variously, appropriately placeless. → See also: Prince of Nysa, Dionysia

O

Object of Desire RA
A term in the First Ientaculum homily. Aurelia distinguishes false goals from happiness, the true object of desire, which requires ordered and deliberate will. Her argument invites comparison with Aquinas’s discussion of happiness in Summa theologiae I–II, q. 2 (111). See also: Final Happiness, Universal Good.
Oblate Sphere SP
Shape of personal starships: a sphere flattened at the poles. Students perch “like big birds on the tops of their oblate spheres which in turn were balanced atop launching needles.” At launch, students “seemed to melt into” them. → See also: Launching Needles, Death-mind
Odor-Signature SP
Identity marker detectable by smell. Aurelia is astonished Earth people lack this sense: “Don’t you know enough to give every character you play a different odor-signature?” she asks Julio. “It’s coming into a blind world or a deaf world.” The Shining People’s governance depends on senses Earth has not developed. → See also: Julio Cordovan, Shining People
Olympians CA
Greek mythology: gods dwelling on Mount Olympus. When serving mulsum, the Prince of Nysa notes: “The Olympians used it.” Aurelia asks if there were Olympians on this world; he replies: “Sort of a Road-Show version of them.” → See also: Mulsum, Prince of Nysa
Operatic-conversevole SP
Italian conversevole: “conversational.” The Shining People’s mode of speaking: voices that are “very carrying” and blend speech with song, carrying between nearby launching needles. → See also: Basso-parlante, Contralto

P

Pan-Math and Science Boluxus ET
James Forcedmarch’s grand title. His conversation with Aurelia moves from the location of Shining World to her electric surface, pointillism, and the relation between inner and outer landscapes (65–69). The grandiose label undercuts any simple division between science, art, and speculation. See also: Forcedmarch, James.
Pandolfo NE
One of the seven students. Encourages Aurelia: “You will be that candle wherever you go, Aurelia. You will be the light of that world.” → See also: Seven Students
Paravata SP
One of the seventy-six planets. Name may derive from Sanskrit paravata (“pigeon”) or parvata (“mountain”). → See also: Seventy-Six Planets
Patmo NE
One of the seven students. Reminds Aurelia of essential preparations: “Don’t forget to set your Compensating Contingency Grid.” Name evokes Patmos, where John received the Revelation. → See also: Seven Students, Compensating Contingency Grid
Patrushkoe-Horse SP
An existing Shining World species that Aurelia’s school-built steed resembled. Students are “not allowed to mimic already existing species too closely.” → See also: Mechano-organo
Peripateticus SP
Latin/Greek: “walking about,” from Aristotle’s teaching habit. Rex’s term for Aurelia’s traveling ministry: “a walkabout, a march, a trek, a trudge, a schola, a forum ambulatory.” → See also: Cavalcade, Circuit-Court
Peter Principle LR
A special-interest advocate who asks Aurelia how to undermine a popular leader. His name alludes to Laurence J. Peter’s principle that people in hierarchies tend to rise to their level of incompetence. Aurelia offers a campaign of excessive, counterfeit praise (51–53). See also: Raw-grab.
Potlatch ET
Northwest Coast indigenous gift-giving ceremony. Rex Golightly’s luxury cabin. “He loves to give gifts and potlatches.” The tent-nature suggests impermanence beneath apparent solidity. → See also: Rex Golightly, Luxury Cabin
Prairie Dog Town Prolocutor PM
“The largest circulation daily in the world.” Reports on Aurelia’s arrival with mixed skepticism and wonder. Combines Western imagery with formal Latin (prolocutor = spokesman). → See also: April Fool
Prandium RM
Latin: Roman midday meal. Second of four daily stops. “The cavalcade formed into a circle of five thousand persons on the grass by the lake-shore.” → See also: Ientaculum, Merenda, Cena
Prince of Nysa NE
A magus and expert in pageants who organizes the ancient festivals surrounding Aurelia’s journey. His name and recollections evoke Dionysus. He says he left the horned people millennia ago and had himself dehorned; he gives his saved horns to Aurelia and Clootie. He also uses athanatos bark and proposes the “Big Blow” cosmology (102, 131–33, 161). See also: Nysa, Big Blow, Athanatos Bark.
Protective Shaft SP
A defensive projection from a student’s ship. Clootie’s shafts intercept deliberate attacks, but a retracting shaft deflects a yin-yang dart into his chest. Aurelia bends over him, blocking the shafts’ access, and the returning dart kills both (179–82). See also: Yin-Yang Yo-Yos, Worm with the Pistol.

R

Ragsdale SP
One of the seventy-six planets, characterized by “juvenile clownishness.” → See also: Seventy-Six Planets, Gelotopolia
Randy Rex Ranch ET
Ranch whose Long-Horn show cattle accompany Aurelia’s cavalcade (109). → See also: Rex Golightly
Raw-grab LN
Corporate takeover technique. Aurelia explains to Kirol Grabman how to create counterpoise companies, manipulate media, pressure churches, kidnap executives. “The raw-grab device is a ‘Wave of the Past.’” → See also: Kirol Grabman, Southern Land Company
Rex Golightly NE
Latin rex: “king.” A tycoon who is “one of the Magi, the first one to appear.” Maintains Potlatch and calls himself “a nomad king.” Represents worldly power attempting to serve transcendent purpose. → See also: Magi, Potlatch, Nomad King
River Boat ET
Floating gambling establishment, also called “River Boat Queen.” “The River Boat goes where it will, on Sea or Lake or Sewer.” Primary setting of the “floating world” where brag is played for blood-stakes. → See also: Floating World, Brag, Helen Staircase
Rome RA
A recurring historical and eschatological marker. Herr Boch says Rome fell two millennia earlier and will rise in another millennium, adding that it has fallen on almost every world (131). The exchange complicates rather than conclusively resolves Aurelia’s planetary identification. See also: World of the Compensation.
Romp Publications PM
Publisher of Will It Ever Be Fun Again? The Aurelian Revival. The name suggests playful or unserious publishing. → See also: Books About Aurelia
Rory McCory NE
The numerologist and mathematician who disputes with Aurelia about a supposed prime number between five and seven. She treats the unnamed number as a corrupting intrusion and associates it with the Number of the Beast. Clootie supports its existence (64–65). See also: Cousin Clootie.
Rotten Ralph’s ET
A “holy-unholy” nightclub for the humanities elite. Walter Kunste invites Aurelia: “Will you join the most illustrious of the rotters at Rotten Ralph’s tonight?” She declines, fearing the Kill Aurelia Now crowd, though they “wouldn’t hinder you, not if they knew that you were going to Rotten Ralph’s.” → See also: Walter Kunste
Roxie ET
A woman in the Kill Aurelia Now League whose appearance Aurelia borrows as a disguise. When the disguise fails, Aurelia redirects the mob toward the real Roxie, who is killed (72, 76–77). → See also: Kill Aurelia Now League, Sheila-be-Damned

S

Sabazius CA
Phrygian/Thracian: god associated with Dionysus, depicted as horned serpent. Among masked figures at the cavalcade: “Sabazius the horned serpent, Silenei with small brow-horns.” → See also: Silenei, Dionysia, Horned People
Sackcloth and Ashes RA
Biblical: traditional garments of mourning and repentance (Jonah 3:6, Matthew 11:21). A “very poor-looking man with a push-cart” vends sackcloth and ashes to penitents during the cavalcade. Karl Talion, Blaise Genet, Helen Staircase, and Michael Strogoff “began to haggle and buy their sack-cloth and ashes, and they talked about the quality of it.” Their purchase signals their defection to Cousin Clootie’s camp; they accept his gospel of repentance over Aurelia’s gospel of joy. → See also: Cousin Clootie, Division of Mission, Corporate Communion
Sad Dog Planet SP
One of the seventy-six possible destinations named in Aurelia’s navigation list (10). See also: Seventy-Six Planets.
Saint Cecelia RA
Patron saint of music. One book asks: Is Aurelia Saint Cecelia?. Whether Aurelia is the saint incarnate connects her to holy musicians. → See also: Bad Music League, Books About Aurelia
Seven Students SP
Aurelia’s classmates departing on Kickoff Night: Aurelia, Rex, Adrian, Audry, Lavender, Pandolfo, Patmo, “four males and three females” sharing “one ‘romantic episode’ soul.” → See also: Kickoff Night, Launching Needles
Seven-Day Sickness ET
Aldous Spencer-Trencher’s diagnosis of Aurelia’s terminal condition: the world’s allergic response to an “intruder.” “Either you must die of the contact, or the local race must. It is simpler for you, having fewer moving parts than the aggregate of the local race, to die.” Confirmed by Doctor Thorgrimsson’s anaphylaxis theory. → See also: Aldous Spencer-Trencher, Doctor Thorgrimsson
Seventy-Six Planets SP
The worlds forming the programmed network of Aurelia’s possible destinations. Twenty-one are named in the initial list, followed by fifty-five others. Her ship cannot escape this network and must land on one of its worlds (9–11). See also: Gaea, Skokumchuck, Kleptis.
Sheila-be-Damned ET
Kill Aurelia Now League member whose appearance Aurelia temporarily assumes. Uses intoxicating “sticks” that cause hallucinations. Her profane name reflects the camp’s nihilistic culture. → See also: Roxie, Kill Aurelia Now League
Shining Mist SP
Altered state Helen Staircase identifies in Aurelia: “She’s not in a fog. . . . She’s in a ‘Shining Mist’ of the alchemists. She is talking from another viewpoint.” Suggests visionary perception beyond ordinary consciousness. → See also: Death-Mind, Aurelia
Shining People SP
Aurelia’s species or civilization, also called “Golden People.” Characterized by: operatic-conversevole voices, aerated flesh, bird bones, ability to build mechano-organo creatures, World Government curriculum. Their name suggests luminosity and moral brightness. → See also: Golden People, Shining World
Shining People Tangency SP
Contact point between Shining World civilization and other worlds. The New Shansi Old Journal editorializes: “We believe in the ‘Shining People Tangency.’ . . . Something splendid has touched us!” Geometric term suggesting worlds touch but don’t interpenetrate. → See also: Shining People
Shining World SP
Aurelia’s home planet, center of a civilization sending young governors to “deficient worlds.” Name is both literal (the world shines) and evaluative (brightness against grubbiness). “‘Shining World’ is like a sunbeam or like quicksilver: it is difficult to nail down.” → See also: Shining People, Golden World Cultus
Silenei CA
Greek: companions of Dionysus, aged satyrs with horse features. Among masked figures: “Silenei with small brow-horns.” → See also: Sabazius, Dionysia
Silly Week ET
The ballad-makers’ composition after the deaths. The people wake “at the same time” and say: “What strange daze have we been in anyhow? . . . Oh, it’s been a silly week!” The governorships reduced to entertainment. → See also: Quick-media World
Sireneca SP
One of the seventy-six planets, “pretty distant.” Name combines “Siren” with Latin suffix: a world of dangerous allure. → See also: Seventy-Six Planets
Skokumchuck SP
Chinook Jargon: “strong water.” “The Shelni Planet,” one of the seventy-six. Appears in the students’ World Government Ballad: “From Hound-Dog Hulk to Skokumchuck.” → See also: Seventy-Six Planets
Sky-Rope SP
An image in the Third Prandium homily: choosing a future goal resembles throwing a rope into the sky and climbing it in confidence that it will hold. This is distinct from the monkey’s invisible ladder to Aurelia’s ship (164). See also: Monkey, Home Free Certificate.
Slowpoke Snails ET
Aldous Spencer-Trencher brings Aurelia a bowl at the Third Ientaculum. She feeds five thousand regular followers and others from it, then discards what remains. A thousand kilos arrive at the Third Prandium. Later the narrator identifies snails as a dish the Media Extinction Arm may have poisoned (158–59, 164, 173). See also: Aldous Spencer-Trencher, Media Extinction Arm.
Spartan Dining ET
Feature of Rex’s luxury cabin: “the ancient Spartan dining halls would sit three hundred persons in the plain elegance that the soldier-princes liked.” Paradox of luxurious austerity. → See also: Potlatch
Spooking Worlds SP
Aurelia’s diagnosis of Earth: “This is one of the ‘spooking worlds.’ . . . You people here are trying to spook me into believing that I will die tonight.” Worlds that kill by collective belief; the prophecy becomes self-fulfilling through social pressure. → See also: Fortune-Tellers, Death
Station KEY PM
Radio station broadcasting reports about Aurelia. Call letters spell a word: key to understanding, or to doors Aurelia opens. → See also: Quick-media World
Strange World Sickness SP
The condition that kills about one in seven students taking the World Government Course. Aurelia recognizes that she is dying of it during the Third Prandium. Aldous Spencer-Trencher describes it as the local world’s rejection of her, and Doctor Thorgrimsson develops the analogy after her death (158, 164, 176–77). See also: Seven-Day Sickness, Doctor Thorgrimsson.
Susan Pishcala NE
News-woman murdered in Clootie’s cavalcade: “a case of unmistaken identity” because Aurelia had used her face as disguise. “She did not have a sweet disposition,” so her death is not mourned. The bodyguard notes they can “discard a used disguise with a free conscience.” → See also: Julio Cordovan, Jimmy Candor
Swampy Junction RA
The place where the “Mystery of Iniquity” house sends us back, “a thousand kilometers and a thousand days” of regression. Symbolic of moral starting-point; sin returns us to square one. → See also: Mystery of Iniquity, Law of Happiness

T

Telluris SP
Latin: “of the Earth.” The Latin name for Earth. Gaea is “called Telluris or the Earth by its natives,” placing Earth within cosmic taxonomy. → See also: Gaea
Through a Glass Darkly RA
Allusion to 1 Corinthians 13:12. Aurelia’s teaching: “That we may see this universal good now only through a glass darkly is not a real objection. That is better than not seeing it at all.” → See also: Father of Lights, Law of Happiness
Tookers ET
A type of bird following Aurelia’s cavalcade. “Birds, tookers, hawks, king birds, grackle, black birds, all followed along in crowds.” Regional dialect or Lafferty coinage. → See also: Cavalcade
Trastevere ET
A Roman district whose name means “across the Tiber.” The Bad Music League’s book identifies Saint Cecelia with this quarter as part of its account of her as a musician (84). See also: Saint Cecelia, Bad Music League.
Trolls Under Bridges RA
Scandinavian folklore. Helen Staircase’s self-description: “We are the people placed here to confound you. . . . We are the trolls who live under the bridges.” The River Boat people as liminal guardians, testing travelers. → See also: River Boat, Helen Staircase

U

Uncle Gifford Redwing NE
“Funny uncle” at Potlatch with predatory designs on Aurelia. She ties an Instrumental Knot in his anatomy, leaving him in extreme pain. The knot cannot be untied until Aurelia leaves this world. → See also: Instrumental Knot, Potlatch
Uncle Silas NE
Also “Uncle Simon.” “Befuddled youth” at Potlatch on “medication or trip-facient,” who tells rambling stories about invading “Bandicoot.” Sleeps across Aurelia’s doorway; found decapitated at dawn. Returns as apparition “ninety percent dead,” explaining Clootie’s decapitation gave him “release,” mercy for the “walking dead.” → See also: Cousin Clootie, Athanatos Bark
Uncles, The ET
Surrogate male relatives at Potlatch. Include Uncle Silas (also called Uncle Simon), who guards Aurelia’s door, and Uncle Gifford Redwing, a “funny uncle” who receives an Instrumental Knot for attempted assault. → See also: Uncle Silas, Uncle Gifford Redwing
United Churchmen for Liberation ET
Religious activist group enlisted in “raw-grab” takeovers. Aurelia explains how to “go to the churches which form the most subservient arm of the media.” Satirical name combining ecumenism with politics. → See also: Raw-grab
Universal Good RA
Aurelia’s name for the object of final happiness, which she places “outside-and-above.” She says that seeing this good “through a glass darkly” is better than not seeing it at all, recalling 1 Corinthians 13:12 (111). See also: Final Happiness, Object of Desire.

V

Vaunt-songs SP
The boastful hymns the seven students sing on Kickoff Night before their departures. “They all meditated and prayed. And they sang some more.” The songs combine prayer with self-glorification, appropriate for students who believe themselves incapable of failure. The opening ballad ranges “From Hound-Dog Hulk to Skokumchuck.” The term “vaunt” (to boast) captures the Shining People’s confident, perhaps overconfident, culture. → See also: Kickoff Night, Seven Students, Launching Needles
Vengeance RA
A surly woman warns: “The yin-yang principle takes death-vengeance on those who believe it to be of very small importance.” Aurelia dismisses yin-yang yo-yos but the vengeance proves real; she dies by yin-yang dart. → See also: Yin-Yang Yo-Yos
Virgo CA
Latin: “the Virgin.” Constellation visible in daylight during Aurelia’s cavalcade: “the Hyades, the Waggoner, Virgo.” Associated with harvest and virginity. → See also: Hyades, Waggoner

W

Waggoner CA
Auriga, the Charioteer constellation. Visible in daylight during Aurelia’s cavalcade, suggesting celestial sanction and vehicular protection. → See also: Hyades, Virgo
Walking Dead RA
Uncle Silas’s posthumous description of his condition before Cousin Clootie decapitated him: “I was probably ninety percent dead and decayed.” In Clootie’s home world, “the cutting-off-of-the-head had something to do with dispatching the ‘walking dead’ and giving them release.” The concept suggests that physical life can persist after spiritual death, and that Clootie’s grim ministry involves releasing such unfortunates. The “walking dead” may be those who have rejected happiness and exist in moral decay while technically alive. → See also: Uncle Silas, Cousin Clootie, Division of Mission
Walter Kunste NE
German Kunst: “art.” “High Honcho of the Humanities” who discusses discordancy theory. Appreciates Shining People’s cacophonous horns. “Not even on the Main-Stream. . . . He was on the Rotten River which is somehow larger.” → See also: Bad Music League, Rotten Ralph’s
Waterloo ET
Iowa city in which Hawk-Eye’s Aurelia Is from Iowa: The Waterloo Revelations claims Aurelia was born sixteen years earlier. Albert Derby accepts the documents as genuine but rejects the book’s conclusion, calling it an “over-documented thesis” (82–83). → See also: Iowa, Iowa Double, Hawk-Eye the Reporter
Wax Figures ET
Cf. voodoo dolls; sympathetic magic. On the River Boat, replicas of all international personages, including Aurelia. “It is believed that if you injure them, their primaries will receive the same injury.” Aurelia wonders if she was her wax replica on the first night: “I smelled waxy then.” → See also: River Boat
Wide Awake PM
“The Morning Medical Journal” where Doctor Thorgrimsson publishes his comments on Aurelia’s visit: “The best thing about this curious encounter is that we may be able to learn something from it.” → See also: Doctor Thorgrimsson
Wolf-Children ET
Media phenomenon contextualizing Aurelia’s arrival. The Morning Perspective compares “Sky-Wolf Children” to “Bangia Wolf-Children” and “Little Green Wolf-Children of Lothogoth,” trivializing cosmic visitation as one more media spectacle. → See also: Quick-media World
Words on Water RA
Cf. Keats’s epitaph: “Here lies one whose name was writ in water.” Rex commands his fish projection: “Write this on the water! Preserve her name. Her name is Aurelia.” The words “did not fade,” reversing Keats’s image of oblivion. But fishermen think it’s a “Monumental Water Company” product. → See also: Rex Golightly, Ego-Fragment Projection
World Government Course SP
The tenth-form assignment requiring Shining People students to build ships, travel to other worlds, and govern for several equivalent months before writing a thesis. Clootie says his own people imitate the course and correct its Shining World errors (2, 7, 145–46). See also: Kickoff Night, Cousin Clootie.
World International Press PM
George Clavicle’s employer. Grandiose name suggesting global reach and authority. → See also: George Clavicle
World of the Compensation RA
Herr Boch’s designation for the visited world, which he insists is the only one where the Compensation has occurred. Aurelia knows several other worlds making the same claim. The term suggests Christian redemption, but the disputed planetary naming remains unresolved (131). See also: Compensation, The; Rome.
Worm with the Pistol ET
Marshal-Julio describes a theoretical attack from an extremely low angle that could evade Aurelia’s shielding if she bent over it. The image becomes a rumor, then a painted design on the yin-yang darts. Aurelia recognizes that design in the weapon lodged in Clootie before it strikes her (142, 172, 180). See also: Protective Shaft, Yin-Yang Yo-Yos.

Y

Yellow Dog SP
One of the seventy-six planets. “The perversity of Yellow Dog . . . was well known.” Colloquial name (a yellow dog is a coward or worthless thing) suggests moral deficiency. → See also: Seventy-Six Planets
Yin-Yang Yo-Yos ET
Double-pointed darts that strike selected targets and return to their manipulators on a whistle. Their purported safety depends on contact with earthly materials and people. A collision with Clootie’s unearthly protective shaft defeats that assurance; the dart strikes him and then Aurelia as she bends over him (172, 180–82). See also: Protective Shaft, Worm with the Pistol.

Z

Zero Equation SP
Clootie’s claim that existence begins at zero and returns to zero, with time eventually reversing and erasing the apparent activity between. He offers it during Greenpasture’s speculative discussion of the Big Bang (56). See also: Cousin Clootie, Charles Greenpasture.
